name: Gimhae International Airport
before:
The airport for Busan, South Korea's second city, at the western end of the city. It carried 17,064,613 passengers in 2018.

The constraint here is hard and permanent. The airport is beyond its design capacity and hemmed in by mountains and buildings with nowhere to expand, so a replacement is being built on Gadeokdo to meet demand. One of its two runways, 18L/36R, is reserved for military use by Gimhae Air Base, though there are plans to open it to airliners.

Because the site is shared with the military, photography and video of the apron, runway and military areas is prohibited under the airport's own rules. Worth telling a client who likes taking pictures from the window.

It is the main hub for Air Busan and Korean Air and an operating base for Jeju Air and Jin Air.

The Busan-Gimhae Light Rail has a station at the airport.

It opened in August 1976 and a new international terminal followed on 31 October 2007. The name comes from the nearby city of Gimhae, not Busan, which is why the code PUS and the name do not match.
after:
The airport for Busan, South Korea's second city, in the Gangseo district at the western end of the city.

It moved to this site in August 1976, and a new international terminal opened in October 2007. The name comes from the neighbouring city of Gimhae, not Busan, which is why it does not match the code PUS.
